subject: general
question: If the radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is decreased by 28% and its height is increased by 114%, then what is the percentage increase (rounded off to the nearest integer) in its volume?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume ∝ r²h

Radius ↓ 28% → r = 0.72r

Height ↑ 114% → h = 2.14h

New volume factor = (0.72)² × 2.14

= 0.5184 × 2.14 ≈ 1.109

Increase = 1.109 − 1 = 0.109 = 10.9%

**∴ Answer ≈ 11% increase**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius decreases by 28% and height increases by 114%

**Concept Used:**

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

**Calculation:**

⇒ New radius = 0.72r

⇒ New height = 2.14h

⇒ New volume = π × (0.72r)² × (2.14h)

⇒ = πr²h × (0.72)² × 2.14

⇒ = πr²h × 0.5184 × 2.14

⇒ = πr²h × 1.109

⇒ Increase = (1.109 − 1) × 100

⇒ = 10.9% ≈ 11%

**∴ The percentage increase in volume is 11%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Relation

Volume of cylinder depends on r² and h.

Percentage Change

Convert percentage into multiplier form (1 ± change).

Successive Change

Apply changes step-by-step on each dimension.

Key Insight

Radius impacts volume more as it is squared.
